body: Ok, the issue does definitely seem to occur because the children of the internally copied nodes have different ownership (probably unowned). Since this discovery, I found a couple workarounds (a little annoying though): Option 1. (probably best) - Set the owner of not only the copied node, but also all of its children recursively. Option 2. - If the children of the copied node are not critical for the editor, remove the offending children from the copies (but only in the editor, so gameplay doesn't break). In my case, because this scene is inherited from a .glb import with a collider, the only child of the MeshInstance3D is a StaticBody3D with a CollisionShape3D child, neither of which are critical in the editor. ### For #1: ```gdscript # ... var copy = cube.duplicate() copies.append(copy) add_child(copy) recursive_set_owner(copy) # ... func recursive_set_owner(node: Node) -> void: node.owner = self for child in node.get_children(): recursive_set_owner(child) ``` (Works, but seems like a bit of overhead if the copied scene graph is complex.) ### For #2: ```gdscript # ... var copy = cube.duplicate() copies.append(copy) add_child(copy) copy.owner = self # remove children when in the editor if Engine.is_editor_hint(): for child in copy.get_children(): copy.remove_child(child) # ... ``` (Again works, but only if the children of the copied nodes are unimportant.)

Any update? The reproduction project I attached, along with the provided steps, consistently reproduces the error. If it needs 'testing' it really should not be hard to do. Is there someone specific that needs to test it?

I also provided what I believe to be the source of the problem. If there's more I can do, please ask.
I suppose I can write a PR, but I just don't have the facilities right now to compile / test the change to prove that that is the offending line.

Thanks!
